flawed_step: Lines 48–53 incorrectly claim that α ≤ 1/2 − 1/n is violated for every fixed α>0 when n is sufficiently large; consequently Lemma 1 is false.
counterexample: Let n=10, α=0.3, and let G be the disjoint union of K9 and one isolated vertex x. Every 5-vertex set S contains at least four vertices of K9, so N(S) is exactly the nine K9 vertices. Thus |N(S)|=9≥5+0.3·10=8, satisfying the hypothesis. But deg(x)=0≤3=αn, contradicting the relied-upon claim δ(G)>αn.
assessment_summary: The explicit graph satisfies the stated expansion property but refutes the minimum-degree lemma used in the inductive path construction.
